The statute will most likely be declared unconstitutional because the 7% signature requirement for independents and political body nominees is unusually burdensome and severely restricts ballot access without adequate justification. However, the note's claim that all ballot access restrictions are automatically invalidated is incorrect—courts apply a balancing test under *Anderson v. Celebrezze*, weighing the burden on candidates and voters against the state's regulatory interests. Thus, the high signature requirement likely fails that balancing, but not due to automatic invalidation.
CONFIDENCE: 85
